findings_and_open_questions.kind: recovered tactical duplicate-name question, newly traced current support
findings_and_open_questions.historical_relationship: 059 queue index 1284 leaves AuthoredRigJoint/MhrBone uniqueness and equipment binding policy pending. The 6533-to-95e tactical skin support body changed, so this current trace is a new assessment, not a reassignment of the historical review or proof of an exact new finding alias.
findings_and_open_questions.condition_and_reasoning: The documented first-match ordinal follows index_in/require_in and is supported by their source. Tactical equipment instead builds a per-owner HashMap from cached exact names to Bevy entities. If two queried bones for the same owner have the same label, the later insertion replaces the earlier entry and subsequent lookup selects the retained entity; there is no ordinal tie-break in this path.
findings_and_open_questions.limits: Requires duplicate same-owner labels to reach the tactical query; ordinary scene admission and ECS iteration/order policy were not fully established. Do not claim the README scoped index_in statement is false, or that a runtime misbinding was observed.
findings_and_open_questions.future_repair_acceptance: Establish whether tactical admission rejects duplicate names or retains explicit ordered joint identity through equipment binding. Later exercise the chosen duplicate policy with the actual scene/rig lifecycle and correct owner.

findings_and_open_questions.kind: documentation qualification and open owner reconciliation
findings_and_open_questions.historical_relationship: Original 059 segovb READ-L12-770 explicitly marked README lines 42–43 as application-policy language rather than proof that shared names own parent/weight/animation state. Prior Adler READ-L11-374 preserved open labels and first-match semantics.
findings_and_open_questions.condition_and_reasoning: Current source supports exact string identity, first-match lookup, typed order and checked native u32 packing. RigJointTable does not prove that two columns belong to the same rig; export retains parent values in a separate table, RigInfluences holds weights, and tactical role classification is application-owned. The README final paragraph should be read with these owner boundaries rather than as proof that the label type validates an entire skeleton.
findings_and_open_questions.limits: This is a qualified wording/ownership question, not proof that the text causes a product failure or that all application consumers satisfy the contract. Full call graph, packed data coherence and alias decisions remain open.
findings_and_open_questions.future_repair_acceptance: If the connected audit finds ambiguous owner expectations, make the README explicitly identify which type retains each value and which application validates cross-column membership; keep exact open-label and checked-encoding semantics.

findings_and_open_questions.kind: recovered finding relevant to documented skin-weight boundary
findings_and_open_questions.historical_relationship: 059 q175 and q436 SEGOVB-L12-CONNECTED-RIG-STRONGEST-FOUR-ZERO-SUM-POLICY remain historical records with central alias reconciliation; prior separate rig-skin report is supplemental, not this delegate’s source-read credit.
findings_and_open_questions.condition_and_reasoning: Current strongest_four aggregates raw f32 weights and divides retained values by their sum without checking finite positive normalization. With a nonempty influence row whose weights are all zero, the source reaches zero divided by zero if called.
findings_and_open_questions.limits: No execution, malformed input creation or ordinary application producer proven. Empty WIDTH=0 has no division loop and should not be conflated with a nonempty zero-sum row.
findings_and_open_questions.future_repair_acceptance: Define finite admissible weights, duplicate handling and zero-sum policy at the owning skin boundary before division, with later product validation separate.
